video_title: Chandler Parsons on how HOSTILE the Euroleague is and how Rudy Gobert was BAD at 16 🤣

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on pre-draft workout grind and first-round draft expectations
quotes.excerpt: I remember I was like, damn, this is exhausting, but I loved going there and doing that.
quotes.quote: I remember I was like, damn, this is exhausting, but I loved going there and doing that. And you kind of know, you have an idea like, all right, I killed that workout, all this dude busted my ass. And Houston was kind of a workout that I had where I did really, really well, and I had an idea that they're going to draft me, but I thought they're going to use their earlier pick for me. But yeah, that process was crazy because 19 workouts and talking in one summer was nuts. You're being SEC Player of the Year, you thinking first round. Is Mark telling you that at the time? Yeah, 100%. He was saying like, and I was expecting like, I was supposed to go lottery or something, but he said anywhere from 15 to like 28 was my range. And so I'm like, that's cool, and obviously I was a senior, and this is before you can play 12 years in college now. But like, yeah, I went, I went through the process. I had some great workouts, I had some teams and situations and fits that I knew that would be a great fit for me. And then I just remember draft night comes around, and I didn't go to the draft, I wasn't invited to go to the draft, and so I just had like a party at my house in Orlando with my friends and family. You want to be a first-round pick too because it's guaranteed, right? You don't know.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons' devastation after not being a first-round pick
quotes.excerpt: First round ends and I'm devastated. And Houston was obviously ended up taking me.
quotes.quote: First round ends and I'm devastated. And Houston was obviously ended up taking me, but they had two first-round picks. And they ended up taking Morris Twin and this Lithuanian dude. And I was like, damn, and Mark's calling me all the time and kind of telling me like, hey, don't worry, don't worry. And then I remember he called me on like the 35th pick, and I'm like, you know, your phone rings, you like, it's go time. And he said, hey, if Charlotte doesn't take you the next pick, Houston's going to buy the pick and pay up. And so I was like, all right, great. Charlotte didn't take me. Houston ended up paying like, I remember it was like a record at the time, they paid like $4 million for the pick and took me 38th.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on playing in EuroLeague during the NBA lockout
quotes.excerpt: I went and played in the EuroLeague for three months. I played in this team called Cholet.
quotes.quote: Bro. So how about you finally make your lifelong dream, you get drafted, and then there's no season. And all you rich motherfuckers that have all the contracts are holding out, and I'm sitting here poor in the second. And so it was so frustrating into where I went and played, I went and played in the EuroLeague for three months. I played in this team called Cholet, they were in France, which is crazy looking back on it. We had this big goofy gangly ass 16-year-old kid on our team, it was Rudy Gobert. And he was like this up and coming French kid, and I remember they were like, this kid's going to be the next big deal, and I was like, no, he's not. Like he could barely catch the ball. Obviously he turned into who he was, but yeah, so we played there. I played there for three months, and then just kind of that whole process of traveling, seeing the world. I had never been to Europe before. I went to like 12 different countries playing in the highest league over there, second best league in the world outside the NBA. So that was cool.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on EuroLeague's tough travel and physical play
quotes.excerpt: The travel is so bad. Like you're on long bus rides, you're flying like commercial.
quotes.quote: It was crazy. It was. And I'm talking, I was great that it happened before the league because you go over there and you hear the EuroLeague, it's great, it's competitive. Bro, the travel is so bad. Like you're on long bus rides, you're flying like commercial. It's the fact that you did that and then I got to go to the NBA instead of the other way around was very, it was nice. It was humbling. It was like, okay, there's no way I want to do this shit. I have to do whatever it takes to make it in the league because this ain't for me.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on EuroLeague's different rules and physical play
quotes.excerpt: They don't call defensive three seconds. There's no goaltending. They call carry on everything.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: What you was averaging over there, kid?

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: You know what, the first month, bro, that's a different game, TA. Like there's they don't call, uh, there's no defensive three seconds. There's no goaltending. They call carry on everything. So I remember the first couple weeks, I was garbage. I was so bad, I couldn't adjust to the game. Physical as a motherfucker, they don't call hand checks over there. So it is a completely different game. And so I remember I was obviously the NBA signing that they got, and I was starting. This coach took me out of the starting lineup. I remember he didn't play me one game. There was a real learning curve.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons' EuroLeague struggles and subsequent NBA starting role
quotes.excerpt: I was in great shape. So when training camp happened, I was ready to go.
quotes.quote: And then something clicked where I started cooking. I remember my last month or two. And by the way, when you're playing bad over there, I'm a second-round pick, I'm like, shit. Houston's watching this. They're not going to sign me. Because the lockout happened, now I'm never going to play in the NBA because I didn't go first round, my shit's not guaranteed. So that was kind of just a crazy process for me, but it ended up helping me because my last month, month and a half, I end up cooking. And when the lockout ended, I came back to Houston, and nobody else on Houston had went and played overseas. So now I'm this young kid that's coming back to the NBA, and I was just playing against grown ass men for three months. I was in great shape. So when training camp happened, I was ready to go, and I end up starting like my fifth game of my career. So it was awesome. A month before I was getting benched in the EuroLeague, starting in the NBA a month later.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on hostile European basketball fans throwing objects
quotes.excerpt: They were throwing batteries at me. Like hard ass batteries. Speaking languages you don't know.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Bro, they're through. So one game, we played in, uh, the Greek team, I forgot what they're called, but there's like SWAT team around the stadium, and those fans, bro. First of all, they're smoking cigarettes, it's nuts. They threw they were throwing batteries at me. Like hard ass batteries. Speaking languages you don't know, but you know it's not nice when they. And I played in France too. I was like this NBA player, I just got drafted. So when I was struggling too, they'll let you know too. They're so passionate over there, which is part of the culture that I loved and stuff and being a part of that, but yeah, there were some crazy ass fans over there throwing shit, drinks, food, batteries. And again, like there was one time, there was little like a SWAT team around where there was felt like there was like fireworks going off in the crowd and shit. It's a different world.
